column1: # Coverage status for every builtin in src/builtins.rs.
#   - the name set here must equal the name set in src/builtins.rs, so a
#     builtin cannot be added to the compiler and quietly left untested;
#   - every COVERED builtin must actually be called by a driver in tests/stdlib;
#   - every UNUSABLE builtin is re-probed on each run, so one that starts
#     working goes XPASS instead of staying silently recorded as broken.
#   COVERED           called and asserted by a tests/stdlib driver
#   NEGATIVE_CONTROL  cannot appear in a passing program; proved in Phase 0
#   UNUSABLE          rejected by gcc; `detail` is the probe body that proves it
# THE SIX UNUSABLE BUILTINS ARE A REAL DEFECT, not a gap in these tests.
# src/builtins.rs declares the file-handle family as taking/returning I64, but
# runtime/pd_prelude.h:227-250 declares the same functions over
# `FileHandle` (aka `void*`). Any program that calls one dies in gcc with
# "incompatible integer to pointer conversion passing 'int' to parameter of
# type 'FileHandle'". They type-check and borrow-check cleanly first, so the
# canonical-table tests in src/builtins.rs do not see it: the "one table"
# invariant is enforced between typeck and the borrow checker, but nothing
# checks the table against the C runtime's signatures. This is the D2 drift
# class one layer down. Reported, not fixed, in this change.

column3: aborts; proved by Phase 0 of the gate
